name: Uber
description: Uber runs a marketplace that connects riders, diners, shippers and drivers, couriers and carriers, and keeps a fee on each transaction. In Q2 2026 people spent $58.0B on the platform (gross bookings); Uber's revenue was $14.2B, about a quarter of that. Mobility (rides) is half of bookings and Delivery (Uber Eats and grocery and retail delivery) almost as large; Freight is small at 2.7 percent of bookings. Both big segments earn most of the profit. Uber's stated profit measure, adjusted EBITDA, was $2.8B in Q2 2026 (4.9 percent of bookings), and free cash flow exceeded $10B over the last twelve months. The biggest strategic risk and opportunity is self-driving vehicles: Waymo, Uber's partner in Austin and Atlanta, will launch its own app there in January 2028 and end exclusivity.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label from general knowledge; not checked against an MSCI/S&P source. Uber owns almost no vehicles: it is a fee-taking marketplace, so the Transportation box says little about how it earns.

hq.note: From general knowledge; not re-read from the 10-K cover.

businessLines.name: Mobility
businessLines.how: Uber keeps a commission on each ride booked (revenue was about 25 percent of Mobility gross bookings, computed) from a driver-supplied fleet; rides come from more trips, pricing and product mix.

operatingProfit.note: The figure was extracted as 'segment operating income'; Uber's segment profit measure is normally segment adjusted EBITDA, which the three figures (2,215 + 1,055 - 24 = 3,246 before corporate costs, against total adjusted EBITDA of about $2.8B) fit. Treat as segment adjusted EBITDA until confirmed from the release.

businessLines.name: Delivery
businessLines.how: Uber takes a commission from restaurants and merchants plus delivery fees from customers, and sells advertising to merchants; revenue was about 19 percent of Delivery gross bookings (computed).

operatingProfit.note: See Mobility note on the label

businessLines.marketShare: Uber Eats about 23% of US food delivery; DoorDash 56%, Grubhub 16% (2026)

businessLines.name: Freight
businessLines.how: Uber Freight brokers truckload shipments between shippers and carriers and books the whole freight bill as revenue (revenue is about equal to gross bookings), earning a thin margin between what shippers pay and carriers are paid.

operatingProfit.note: See Mobility note on the label

brands.name: Uber Eats and grocery and retail delivery
